description: Find design nodes by what they say, when you don't know their ids — 'what does the design say about persistence?', 'is there already a requirement about latency?'. BM25 keyword search over every field a node's prose is written in (name, statement, description, a rationale, a change's summary, a check's findings, an interface's spec ...; never an id, date, hash, path or where a record came from), ranked, optionally scoped to one node type. Search BEFORE creating a node that might already exist, and to map the user's words to the node they mean. Result reports its own bounds: hits.len() == limit means there may be more, and a non-empty `stale` list means the index has drifted from the store. Each hit also lists, under `linked`, the records directly linked to it (a review relation or DECOMPOSES, with the direction), so a linked family comes back together even where only one of its records carries your words. On a design that pins others (a hub), `tracked_designs: true` searches them too, from their committed exports. Ask for this to find out whether anyone has written something down about a subject, such as budgets.

limit.description:
Maximum hits to return, best first (default 10). The result echoes it —
hits.len() == limit means there may be more.

node_type.description: Restrict hits to one node type (e.g. "Requirement"); omit for all.

query.description:
Keywords to search for — tokenized BM25 over every field a node's prose
is written in: name, statement, description, a rationale, a change's
summary ... (not substring or regex). Use the words the design would
use: "persistence", "dedup window", "latency budget".

tracked_designs.description:
Also search every design this one PINS (external_dependency with a
graph_id), read-only from each pin's committed export on this machine:
one ranked list, each hit naming its `design`, a pinned design's
node_id carrying its graph_id as a prefix ('<graph_id>:<id>', which
get_node opens). Every pinned design NOT searched is named in
`not_searched` with its `state` and why, so "nothing found" never reads
as nothing anywhere. Default false: this design alone.

name: search_design

outputSchema.description: A ranked list of design nodes matching the query, with the bounds of the search stated so a caller can tell a complete answer from a truncated one.

designs_searched.description: On a search over several designs: the graph_id of each design searched, this one first. `found_by_design`, `searched_by_design` and `hits_withheld` give each one's count and what the one `limit` left out; with `tracked_designs`, `read_from` names the export each pinned design was read from.

hits.description: Matching nodes, best first. Scores are comparable WITHIN one result list and not across queries.

age_days.description: Present only on a node carrying a date — how old its claim is. Absent on an undated node.

as_of.description: The date the claim was made, when it carries one.

design.description: Present on a search over several designs (`tracked_designs`, or a hub's address): the graph_id of the design this hit is in.

linked.description: Records directly linked to this hit by a review relation or DECOMPOSES, at most 8. LINKED, not matched: they need not contain the query. Absent when nothing is linked.

direction.description: `out`: hit RELATION linked. `in`: linked RELATION hit.

name.description: The node's name at hit time; empty if it has none.

limit.description: The limit that bounded this result. hits.len() == limit means there may be more; this is the no-silent-caps rule made visible.

loop_hint.description: Present only when the coherence loop is owed something.

not_searched.description: Present only on a design that pins other designs (external_dependency with a graph_id): each pinned design this search did NOT look in, with where it could be read and why it was not searched. A hit missing here says nothing about them.

read_at.description: `export` (a path) or `address`; empty when the pin names neither.

state.description: With `tracked_designs`: why it was not searched, in one word — `missing`, `unreadable`, `not_reached` (at an address), `nowhere`, `not_read` (past the read cap) or `not_followed` (pinned by a pinned design).

not_searched_note.description: Beside `not_searched`: how many pinned designs were not looked in.

searched.description: How many of the design's nodes the search ran over (the search index's own count). It says WHICH empty an empty `hits` is: nothing matched among this many.

stale.description: Ids the index returned but the store no longer holds. NON-EMPTY MEANS THE INDEX HAS DRIFTED and a reindex is due — it is not a list of results.

tracked_note.description: With `tracked_designs`, when it added nothing: why.

title: Search the Design
